title: How data centres became the sleeper issue that could decide the US midterms
key_facts: Community groups organising against data centers more than doubled to 833 in the first months of this year, per Data Center Watch.
About 3,000 data centers operate in the US and the number could double in a few years, per Pew Research Center.
Trump called the backlash a 'sick conspiracy' and said people keeping data centers out are 'backwards and poor'.
Arizona Governor Katie Hobbs enacted a three-year pause on new data center tax breaks in July.
Republican Senator John Husted of Ohio softened his support as polls show Ohio voters oppose data centers.
Brookings: a new data center creates 100 to 200 local jobs and has essentially no impact on local wages.
Most moratoriums end in one to three years.
quote_evidence: "This has become a sleeper issue for the entire election cycle", the NRSC added.
It is possible that the political winds will have shifted by the time such moratoriums expire, leaving Big Tech and AI firms to build as they wish.
why_it_matters_hint: Local anger has turned data centers into a national election issue.
